entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8131"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 9</title> <div sID="gen12668" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Eccl.9.1-Eccl.9.18">Ec 9:1-18</reference>.<div eID="gen12668" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12669" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8131"/><hi type="bold">1. declare--</hi>rather, explore; the result of my exploring is this, that "the righteous, &c., are in the hand of God. No man knoweth either the love or hatred (of God to them) by all that is before them," that is, by what is outwardly seen in His present dealings (<reference osisRef="Eccl.8.14">Ec 8:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eccl.8.17">17</reference>). However, from the sense of the same words, in <reference osisRef="Eccl.9.6">Ec 9:6</reference>, "love and hatred" seem to be the feelings of the wicked towards the righteous, whereby they caused to the latter comfort or sorrow. Translate: "Even the love and hatred" (exhibited towards the righteous, are in God's hand) (<reference osisRef="Ps.76.10">Psa 76:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.16.7">Pr 16:7</reference>). "No man knoweth all that is before them." <div eID="gen12669" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_plain: 2. All things ... alike-- not universally; but as to death. Ec 9:2-10 are made by Holden the objection of a skeptical sensualist. However, they may be explained as Solomon's language. He repeats the sentiment already implied in Ec 2:14 ; 3:20; 8:14 . one event-- not eternally; but death is common to all. good-- morally. clean-- ceremonially. sacrificeth-- alike to Josiah who sacrificed to God, and to Ahab who made sacrifice to Him cease. sweareth-- rashly and falsely.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8136"/><div sID="gen12687" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8136"/><hi type="bold">6. love, and ... hatred, &c.--</hi>(referring to <reference osisRef="Eccl.9.1">Ec 9:1</reference>; see on <reference osisRef="Eccl.9.1">Ec 9:1</reference>). Not that these cease in a future world absolutely (<reference osisRef="Ezek.32.27">Eze 32:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.11">Re 22:11</reference>); but as the end of this verse shows, relatively to persons and things in this world. Man's love and hatred can no longer be exercised for good or evil in the same way as here; but the fruits of them remain. What he is at death he remains for ever. "Envy," too, marks the wicked as referred to, since it was therewith that they assailed the righteous (see on <reference osisRef="Eccl.9.1">Ec 9:1</reference>).<div eID="gen12687" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12688" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">portion--</hi>Their "portion" was "in this life" (<reference osisRef="Ps.17.14">Psa 17:14</reference>), that they now "cannot have any more." <div eID="gen12688" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 6. love, and ... hatred, &c.-- (referring to Ec 9:1 ; see on Ec 9:1 ). Not that these cease in a future world absolutely ( Eze 32:27 ; Re 22:11 ); but as the end of this verse shows, relatively to persons and things in this world. Man's love and hatred can no longer be exercised for good or evil in the same way as here; but the fruits of them remain. What he is at death he remains for ever. "Envy," too, marks the wicked as referred to, since it was therewith that they assailed the righteous (see on Ec 9:1 ). portion-- Their "portion" was "in this life" ( Psa 17:14 ), that they now "cannot have any more."

Being "in the hand of God," who now accepteth "thy works" in His service, as He has previously accepted thy person (<reference osisRef="Gen.4.4">Ge 4:4</reference>), thou mayest "eat ... with a cheerful (not sensually 'merry') heart" (<reference osisRef="Eccl.3.13">Ec 3:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eccl.5.18">5:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.2.46">Ac 2:46</reference>). <div eID="gen12689" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8138"/><div sID="gen12690" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8138"/><hi type="bold">8. white--</hi>in token of joy (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.3">Is 61:3</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8141"/><div sID="gen12697" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8141"/>11. This verse qualifies the sentiment, <reference osisRef="Eccl.9.7-Eccl.9.9">Ec 9:7-9</reference>. Earthly "enjoyments," however lawful in their place (<reference osisRef="Eccl.3.1">Ec 3:1</reference>), are to give way when any work to be done for God requires it. Reverting to the sentiment (<reference osisRef="Eccl.8.17">Ec 8:17</reference>), we ought, therefore, not only to work God's work "with might" (<reference osisRef="Eccl.9.10">Ec 9:10</reference>), but also with the feeling that the event is wholly "in God's hand" (<reference osisRef="Eccl.9.1">Ec 9:1</reference>).<div eID="gen12697" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12698" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">race ... not to the swift--</hi>(<reference osisRef="2Sam.18.23">2Sa 18:23</reference>); spiritually (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.19">Zep 3:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.9.16">Ro 9:16</reference>).<div eID="gen12698" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12699" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">nor ... battle to ... strong--</hi>(<reference osisRef="1Sam.17.47">1Sa 17:47</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.14.9">2Ch 14:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.11.15">11, 15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.33.16">Psa 33:16</reference>).<div eID="gen12699" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12700" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bread--</hi>livelihood.<div eID="gen12700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12701" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">favour--</hi>of the great.<div eID="gen12701" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12702" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">chance--</hi>seemingly, really Providence. But as man cannot "find it out" (<reference osisRef="Eccl.3.11">Ec 3:11</reference>), he needs "with all might" to use opportunities. Duties are ours; events, God's. <div eID="gen12702" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 11. This verse qualifies the sentiment, Ec 9:7-9 . Earthly "enjoyments," however lawful in their place ( Ec 3:1 ), are to give way when any work to be done for God requires it. Reverting to the sentiment ( Ec 8:17 ), we ought, therefore, not only to work God's work "with might" ( Ec 9:10 ), but also with the feeling that the event is wholly "in God's hand" ( Ec 9:1 ). race ... not to the swift-- ( 2Sa 18:23 ); spiritually ( Zep 3:19 ; Ro 9:16 ). nor ... battle to ... strong-- ( 1Sa 17:47 ; 2Ch 14:9 , 11, 15 ; Psa 33:16 ). bread-- livelihood. favour-- of the great. chance-- seemingly, really Providence. But as man cannot "find it out" ( Ec 3:11 ), he needs "with all might" to use opportunities. Duties are ours; events, God's.

Hence the danger of delay in doing the work of God, as one knows not when his opportunity will end ( Ec 9:10 ). evil net-- fatal to them. entries.reader_content_plain: 12. his time-- namely, of death ( Ec 7:15 ; Is 13:22 ). Hence the danger of delay in doing the work of God, as one knows not when his opportunity will end ( Ec 9:10 ). evil net-- fatal to them. The unexpected suddenness of the capture is the point of comparison. So the second coming of Jesus Christ, "as a snare" ( Lu 21:35 ). evil time-- as an "evil net," fatal to them.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8148"/><div sID="gen12715" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8148"/><hi type="bold">18. one sinner, &c.--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Josh.7.1">Jos 7:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.11.12">11, 12</reference>). Though wisdom excels folly (<reference osisRef="Eccl.9.16">Ec 9:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eccl.7.19">7:19</reference>), yet a "little folly (equivalent to sin) can destroy much good," both in himself (<reference osisRef="Eccl.10.1">Ec 10:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jas.2.10">Jas 2:10</reference>) and in others. "Wisdom" must, from the antithesis to "sinner," mean religion. Thus typically, the "little city" may be applied to the Church (<reference osisRef="Luke.12.32">Lu 12:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.12.22">He 12:22</reference>); the great king to Satan (<reference osisRef="John.12.31">Joh 12:31</reference>); the despised poor wise man, Jesus Christ (<reference osisRef="Isa.53.2">Is 53:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.53.3">3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mark.6.3">Mr 6:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.8.9">2Co 8:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.1.7">Ep 1:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.8">8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.2.3">Col 2:3</reference>). <chapter eID="Eccl.9"/>
entries.content_plain: 18. one sinner, &c.-- ( Jos 7:1 , 11, 12 ). Though wisdom excels folly ( Ec 9:16 ; 7:19 ), yet a "little folly (equivalent to sin) can destroy much good," both in himself ( Ec 10:1 ; Jas 2:10 ) and in others. "Wisdom" must, from the antithesis to "sinner," mean religion. Thus typically, the "little city" may be applied to the Church ( Lu 12:32 ; He 12:22 ); the great king to Satan ( Joh 12:31 ); the despised poor wise man, Jesus Christ ( Is 53:2 , 3 ; Mr 6:3 ; 2Co 8:9 ; Ep 1:7 , 8 ; Col 2:3 ).
